title: 2009年考研英语一 Part B · 七选五

sentences: Directions ;
In the following text, some segments have been removed.
For Questions 41-45, choose the most suitable one from the list A-G to fit into each of the numbered blanks.
There are two extra choices, which do not fit in any of the blanks.
Mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET 1. (10 points)
translations: 说明；
在下面的文本中，一些段落已被移除。
对于问题41-45，从列表A-G中选择最合适的一个填入每个编号的空白处。
有两个额外的选项，它们不适合任何空白处。
在答题卡1上标记你的答案。（10分）

sentences: Coinciding with the groundbreaking theory of biological evolution proposed by British naturalist Charles Darwin in the 1860s, British social philosopher Herbert Spencer put forward his own theory of biological and cultural evolution.
Spencer argued that all worldly phenomena, including human societies, changed over time, advancing toward perfection.
translations: 与英国博物学家查尔斯·达尔文在19世纪60年代提出的开创性生物进化理论相吻合，英国社会哲学家赫伯特·斯宾塞提出了他自己的生物和文化进化理论。
斯宾塞认为，所有世俗现象，包括人类社会，都随着时间的推移而变化，朝着完美前进。

sentences: American social scientist Lewis Henry Morgan introduced another theory of cultural evolution in the late 1800s.
Morgan helped found modern anthropology—the scientific study of human societies, customs and beliefs—thus becoming one of the earliest anthropologists.
In his work, he attempted to show how all aspects of culture changed together in the evolution of societies.
translations: 美国社会科学家刘易斯·亨利·摩根在19世纪末引入了另一种文化进化理论。
摩根帮助创立了现代人类学——对人类社会的科学研究，习俗和信仰——从而成为最早的人类学家之一。
在他的工作中，他试图展示文化的所有方面如何在社会的进化中一起变化。

sentences: In the early 1900s in North America, German-born American anthropologist Franz Boas developed a new theory of culture known as historical particularism.
Historical particularism, which emphasized the uniqueness of all cultures, gave new direction to anthropology.
translations: 在20世纪初的北美，德国出生的美国人类学家弗朗茨·博厄斯发展了一种新的文化理论，称为历史特殊主义。
历史特殊主义强调所有文化的独特性，为人类学提供了新的方向。

sentences: Boas felt that the culture of any society must be understood as the result of a unique history and not as one of many cultures belonging to a broader evolutionary stage or type of culture.
translations: 博厄斯认为，任何社会的文化都必须被理解为独特历史的结果，而不是属于更广泛进化阶段或文化类型的众多文化之一。

sentences: Historical particularism became a dominant approach to the study of culture in American anthropology, largely through the influence of many students of Boas.
But a number of anthropologists in the early 1900s also rejected the particularist theory of culture in favor of diffusionism.
Some attributed virtually every important cultural achievement to the inventions of a few, especially gifted peoples that, according to diffusionists, then spread to other cultures.
translations: 历史特殊主义成为美国人类学文化研究的主导方法，主要是通过博厄斯的许多学生的影响。
但在20世纪初，许多人类学家也拒绝了特殊主义文化理论，转而支持传播主义。
一些人几乎将每一项重要的文化成就都归功于少数特别有天赋的民族的发明，根据传播主义者的说法，这些发明随后传播到其他文化。

sentences: Also in the early 1900s, French sociologist Emile Durkheim developed a theory of culture that would greatly influence anthropology.
Durkheim proposed that religious beliefs functioned to reinforce social solidarity.
An interest in the relationship between the function of society and culture became a major theme in European, and especially British, anthropology.
translations: 同样在20世纪初，法国社会学家埃米尔·涂尔干发展了一种文化理论，将极大地影响人类学。
涂尔干提出，宗教信仰的功能是加强社会团结。
对社会功能与文化之间关系的兴趣成为欧洲，尤其是英国人类学的一个主要主题。

sentences: [A] Other anthropologists believed that cultural innovations, such as inventions, had a single origin and passed from society to society.
This theory was known as diffusionism.
translations: [A] 其他人类学家认为，文化创新，如发明，有一个单一的起源，并从一个社会传递到另一个社会。
这种理论被称为传播主义。

sentences: [B] In order to study particular cultures as completely as possible, he became skilled in linguistics, the study of languages, and in physical anthropology, the study of human biology and anatomy.
translations: [B] 为了尽可能完整地研究特定文化，他精通语言学，即对语言的研究，以及体质人类学，即对人类生物学和解剖学的研究。

sentences: [C] He argued that human evolution was characterized by a struggle he called the “survival of the fittest,” in which weaker races and societies must eventually be replaced by stronger, more advanced races and societies.
translations: [C] 他认为，人类进化的特点是他称之为“适者生存”的斗争，在这场斗争中，较弱的种族和社会最终必须被更强、更先进的种族和社会所取代。

sentences: [D] They also focused on important rituals that appeared to preserve a people’s social structure, such as initiation ceremonies that formally signify children’s entrance into adulthood.
translations: [D] 他们还关注似乎能保持一个民族社会结构的重要仪式，例如正式表示儿童进入成年的入会仪式。

sentences: [E] Thus, in his view, diverse aspects of culture, such as the structure of families, forms of marriage, categories of kinship, ownership of property, forms of government, technology, and systems of food production, all changed as societies evolved.
translations: [E] 因此，在他看来，文化的不同方面，如家庭结构、婚姻形式、亲属关系类别、财产所有权、政府形式、技术和食品生产系统，都随着社会的进化而变化。

sentences: [F] Supporters of the theory viewed culture as a collection of integrated parts that work together to keep a society functioning.
translations: [F] 该理论的支持者将文化视为一个由相互整合的部分组成的集合，这些部分共同作用以保持社会运转。

sentences: [G] For example, British anthropologists Grafton Elliot Smith and W. J. Perry incorrectly suggested, on the basis of inadequate information, that farming, pottery making, and metallurgy all originated in ancient Egypt and diffused throughout the world.
In fact, all of these cultural developments occurred separately at different times in many parts of the world.
translations: [G] 例如，英国人类学家格拉夫顿·埃利奥特·史密斯和W. J. 佩里在信息不足的基础上错误地提出，农业、陶器制作和冶金术都起源于古埃及并传播到世界各地。
事实上，所有这些文化发展都在世界许多地方的不同时间分别发生。
